items.item_text: Bachelors degree in Psychology, Neuroscience, or a related field
Experience working with pediatric, neurodevelopment, autism spectrum disorder, or other clinical populations
Minimum 1 year of experience supporting research projects in a laboratory, academic, clinical research, or related research environment
Experience with behavioral, psychophysiological, or neuroimaging research methods
Experience with research databases or electronic data capture systems, such as REDCap

The UCLA Sensory, Cognitive, and Affective Neurodevelopment (SCAN) Laboratory within the Semel Institute for Neuroscience and Human Behavior is seeking a full-time Research Assistant to support innovative research examining sensory processing and neurodevelopment in individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). This position offers hands-on experience in clinical research, neuroimaging, behavioral assessments, and data analysis. Key responsibilities include:
Assist with participant recruitment, screening, scheduling, and study visits
Support implementation of research protocols and maintain study documentation
Collect, manage, and process neuroimaging, behavioral, psychophysiological, and questionnaire-based data
Assist with MRI participant preparation and data acquisition
Support data cleaning, quality control, database management, and analysis
Assist with study reports, presentations, manuscripts, and grant-related analysis
Maintain IRB and regulatory documentation and support general laboratory operations

The department's typical operating hours are Monday through Friday, 8am-6pm. Staff may occasionally be scheduled during evenings or weekend hours based on research participants needs. Employees should expect to work approximately 2-3 weekends per month, with weekday schedules adjusted to maintain a 40-hour workweek.
Comfort working with individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD)
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint
Knowledge of basic research methods and data collection procedures
Knowledge of MRI research procedures, data processing software, or neuroimaging analysis tools
Ability to maintain accurate research records and documentation
Ability to interact professional with research participants and families from diverse backgrounds
Ability to work effectively as part of a multidisciplinary research team
Strong verbal and written communication skills
